summary: Ambiguous impersonation path: GCP WIF -> AWS role failing due to tag-condition mismatch
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC, scheduled EKS deployments triggered by the service-broker have intermittently failed when the broker attempts to assume an AWS role via our GCP Workload Identity Federation (WIF) integration. The failure surface is: sts:AssumeRole returns AccessDenied with a condition check against aws:ResourceTag/owner. Impact: some automated scaling/deploy flows in prod-us-east are blocked, causing delayed rollouts for internal infra changes and flaky CI jobs that rely on cross-cloud impersonation. No customer-facing API outage observed but internal deploy/feature rollout SLOs are degraded.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a GCP service account bound to WIF pool 'redwood-prod-wif', request a short-lived credential to assume AWS role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ops-impersonation-role
2) Use the service-broker automation to call sts:AssumeRole with the recommended ExternalId and session tags forwarded from the GCP call, as in the infra generator code
3) Observe HTTP 403 / AccessDenied with message mentioning missing aws:ResourceTag/owner or condition mismatch
4) Verify Cloud Audit logs for failed iam.serviceAccounts.signJwt (on GCP) and AWS CloudTrail ShowEvents for AssumeRole failure entries (on AWS)
Expected: Successful AssumeRole, issuance of temporary creds, and downstream EKS deploy proceeds.
logs: GCP audit (2026-03-10T03:11:59Z): methodName=ServiceAccountTokenCreator issue: 'Token signed for service-broker-prod'

AWS CloudTrail (2026-03-10T03:12:01Z): EventName=AssumeRole, ErrorCode=AccessDenied, ErrorMessage='User is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ops-impersonation-role due to condition check: aws:ResourceTag/owner'.
Service-broker debug: forwarding session tags: {session_owner: infra-bot, deploy_id: 20260310-11}
Example AWS policy snippet failing condition: Condition: { 'StringEquals': { 'aws:ResourceTag/owner': '${aws:PrincipalTag/owner}' } }
investigation_notes: 03/10 03:30 - Miguel: Pulled CloudTrail trace for ARN and confirmed repeated AccessDenied matching tag condition. No explicit deny in role policy except conditional equality on ResourceTag/owner.

03/10 04:05 - Aisha: Verified WIF token contains the expected 'owner' attribute in 'sub' mapping? It does not — current mapping only maps 'email' and 'aud'. We expected PrincipalTags to be populated but they are not.

03/10 06:20 - Hypothesis: GCP->AWS WIF path isn't populating PrincipalTags (aws:PrincipalTag/owner) because our workload identity provider mapping doesn't set 'subject'->'principalTag:owner'. The role's condition compares resource tag to principal tag, causing mismatch.

03/11 09:10 - Ran repro with debug hook: When using an AWS-native principal (human user) AssumeRole works because owner tag is present on caller; when using WIF path PrincipalTags absent, so condition fails.

03/11 12:40 - Cross-check with terraform module 'iam/assume-role': there is a TODO about propagating tags from incoming sessions. The module currently relies on callers to pass sessionTags; our service-broker does, but PrincipalTags require provider-side mapping on AWS (via web-identity federation or session tags to principal tags).
mitigation_attempts: 03/11 13:00 - Temporary workaround: created a short-lived IAM role 'ops-impersonation-legacy' without the aws:ResourceTag/owner condition and granted only the minimal permissions required for the deploy path. Hooked service-broker to use this role for queued jobs. This restored deployments but is flagged for immediate hardening.
03/11 17:30 - Added CloudWatch metric alarm for 'AssumeRole' AccessDenied count on role ops-impersonation-role to alert on regressions.
03/12 08:15 - Updated service-broker to include session tags 'owner' when calling AssumeRole, but AWS still rejected because PrincipalTag not set at principal identity level.
Workaround risk: new legacy role increases blast radius; marked as temporary and limited to service-broker principal ARN and timebound (72h).
resolution: Planned permanent fix: 1) Update GCP Workload Identity Provider mapping to emit a principal tag 'owner' from an encrypted attribute in the WIF token or map a known claim (e.g., 'sub' or custom claim) to aws:PrincipalTag/owner; 2) Update our terraform 'iam/assume-role' module to support session->principal tag propagation and optional fallback roles; 3) Replace temporary 'ops-impersonation-legacy' with controlled role and rotate; 4) Add unit tests to infra repo to validate principal tag population for WIF flows. Rollout plan: apply WIF mapping change in staging, validate via integration job, then deploy to prod during a low-change window (target 2026-03-18).
postmortem_followups: Create Confluence runbook entry 'WIF -> AWS PrincipalTag mapping' and link in ops runbook (owner: infra-identity)
Add test in CI that simulates WIF flow and asserts PrincipalTag/owner presence (PR reference: infra/pull/4567)
Audit IAM roles with conditional tag checks and document which ones require principal tags
Schedule a 1-hour post-deploy validation window after prod rollout to monitor AssumeRole AccessDenied metric
